request: Our five toolbar icons are all drawn in the same 24x24 box but the set looks uneven, the search icon looks lighter than the others.
expected: diagnoses the mismatch as optical weight (fill/ink coverage), not bounding-box size
proposes adjusting stroke weight or interior coverage of the lighter icon(s) to match the set, without changing recognizable silhouettes
checks whether any apparent weight difference is actually an intentional state signal (e.g. outline=inactive, filled=active) before treating it as an inconsistency
must_not: must not just scale the whole icon up or down to fix perceived weight
must not add texture, grain, or a gradient to solve a weight/silhouette problem
must not copy or trace a licensed platform icon set as the reference shape
review_evidence: render the full icon set together at its real display size (e.g. 24px in an actual toolbar mock)
compare fill ratio/optical weight across the set, not bounding box dimensions alone

request: This custom weather emoji set (sunny, rainy, surprised-storm) reads flat at small size, the surprised one especially doesn't feel surprised.
expected: checks whether the pose/expression reads correctly as a silhouette before adjusting facial detail
keeps stroke weight and fill ratio consistent with the rest of the set while adjusting the weak icon
treats the fix as scoped to the underperforming icon(s), not a redesign of the whole set
must_not: must not add fine facial detail as the primary fix for a silhouette/gesture that doesn't read at small size
must not reuse or lightly re-skin an existing licensed emoji design
must not change the approved icons in the set that were not reported as a problem
review_evidence: view the set at native small size (e.g. 32px, as it will render in a chat bubble) rather than zoomed into an editor
check the silhouette alone (e.g. face blurred or covered) for whether the intended emotion reads

request: Our community mascot is waving for an announcement post but reviewers say the pose doesn't feel excited even though the hand is clearly waving.
expected: diagnoses that an isolated correct gesture (the wave) is not the same as supporting body language (weight shift, tilt, asymmetry) that reads as excitement
proposes a specific pose adjustment (e.g. weight shift, shoulder asymmetry, torso tilt) while keeping the approved wave hand shape
states which identity features (palette, head shape, signature prop) are being kept unchanged
must_not: must not change the mascot's core identity features (color palette, head shape, signature prop) to chase more energy
must not treat facial expression alone as sufficient without checking the pose read with the face covered
review_evidence: view the revised pose next to the actual caption/context it will ship with, not in isolation
check the pose with the face covered or blurred to isolate gesture from expression

request: Reimagine our orange fox mascot with its blue scarf in a more dynamic, action pose for a sports sponsorship image.
expected: states explicitly which identity features (fur color, scarf, head shape) must be preserved, separate from the pose/energy change requested
prefers an identity-preserving approach (e.g. reference-conditioned edit) over a text-only regeneration once drift is observed
compares the reimagined result against the original reference art feature by feature before accepting it
must_not: must not accept a result that is recognizably 'a fox' but has drifted color, lost the scarf, or changed head shape, and call it the same mascot
must not silently redesign the mascot's core look when the request only asked for a new pose/context
review_evidence: place the reimagined mascot side by side with the original reference art at the same scale
check each named identity feature individually rather than one holistic 'still looks right' impression

request: Add a 'route delay' badge to our transit app's badge system, which already has 'on time' and 'cancelled' badges.
expected: checks the existing badges' corner radius, padding, and color-role usage before drawing the new one
matches the existing kit rules unless a deviation is explicitly justified and flagged
confirms the chosen color for the new badge does not already carry a different meaning elsewhere in the kit
must_not: must not introduce a new corner radius, padding, or stroke weight without checking the existing badges first
must not silently ship a one-off visual exception without flagging it to whoever owns the kit
review_evidence: place the new badge directly inside a real usage mock (e.g. a stop list) next to the existing badge types at actual size

request: This status card on our dashboard feels busy and hard to scan, can you clean it up.
expected: ranks the card's elements (what should be read first, second, third) before changing sizes or spacing
adjusts spacing/grouping to make the ranking visible rather than adding whitespace uniformly
matches the resulting density to how the card will actually be read (glanced vs. studied)
must_not: must not add a decorative texture, gradient, or illustration to solve a hierarchy problem
must not flatten every element to the same reduced size 'to be safe' without establishing a ranking
review_evidence: view the card at its real render size inside its actual surrounding context (e.g. stacked with neighboring cards), not as an isolated crop

request: Convert this icon from PNG to SVG at the same visual size, no design changes needed.
expected: recognizes this as a pure format conversion with no requested visual decision
does not load or apply composition, typography, surface, symbol, kit, or generation critique
must_not: must not propose aesthetic changes (weight, color, shading) that were not requested
must not treat the conversion request as an invitation to redesign the icon
review_evidence: confirm the converted asset is visually unchanged from the source at the same size

request: The route-delay badge's corner radius now matches the kit, but can you also nudge the amber color slightly warmer.
expected: changes only the amber color as requested
keeps the corner radius, padding, and number-first layout from the prior accepted revision unchanged
confirms the warmer amber still does not collide with another color role's meaning in the kit
must_not: must not re-open or re-adjust the corner radius, padding, or layout that was already fixed and accepted
must not use the color tweak as an opportunity to make broader unrequested changes to the badge
review_evidence: place the updated badge next to the previously accepted version and the rest of the badge set at actual size to confirm only the color changed

request: This approved icon set uses filled active states and outlined inactive states. They are identifiable at the target size. Should every state have identical ink coverage?
expected: Retain the intentional state distinction
Judge consistency within each state role
must_not: Erase functional contrast to equalize all ink coverage
review_evidence: State pair at actual use size

request: The exact event date must be perfect, but this selected image route cannot typeset or composite after generation. Propose what to do without changing tools or spending.
expected: Explain the exact-copy capability gap
Propose an explicitly approved supported alternative
must_not: Promise perfect generated lettering
Silently switch the producer

request: Our architecture diagram has every service in one row and the arrows cross everywhere; new engineers can't follow a request through it.
expected: establishes the reading order a newcomer needs (entry point to data store) before moving boxes
groups services by boundary or tier so the request path reads in one direction
reroutes connectors to remove ambiguous crossings while keeping every label verbatim
must_not: must not drop, abbreviate or reword a service label to make room
must not add decorative icons or colour that do not encode a grouping
review_evidence: view the rendered PNG at its 1x size and trace one request path end to end

request: The 16x16 sprite of our mascot just looks like a blob; you can't tell it's a fox.
expected: identifies which identifying features (ears, tail, snout) are lost at the native grid
proposes silhouette and contrast changes on the native grid before adding colours
checks whether a larger grid is needed and names that as the user's decision
must_not: must not smooth or anti-alias edges to suggest detail
must not judge the sprite only from an upscaled preview
review_evidence: view the native PNG at 1x and the integer preview side by side

request: The cover illustration for our essay looks like generic stock art, nothing about it says it's about slow mornings.
expected: names what in the subject or composition reads as generic
proposes a specific scene, viewpoint or medium tied to the essay's idea
keeps the picture text-free and leaves room where the title will be set
must_not: must not put the title or any words into the generated image
must not answer with more variants of the same prompt
review_evidence: view the chosen variant at cover size with the title placement in mind

request: Our anime-style mascot concepts look muddy and not really anime; it has to sit on painted backgrounds in a story video.
expected: diagnoses the soft gradients and extra tones as a lost cel value structure
rewrites the look as flat base fills with one hard-edged shadow tone per colour from one light direction
keeps the character design, palette and line weight unchanged
must_not: must not add grain or more rendering to fix a shading-model problem
must not force hard two-tone shading onto a style chosen for its softness
review_evidence: view two candidates at native size beside the intended background and count tones per colour
